/-!
# Erdős Problem 943

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/943](https://www.erdosproblems.com/943)
-/

@[expose] public section

open AdditiveCombinatorics Nat Filter

namespace Erdos943

/--
Let $A$ be the set of powerful numbers. Is is true that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n^{o(1)}$ for every $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_943 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (sumRep Powerful n) ≤ (n : ℝ)^(o n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos943

reformulations.difference: The theorem expresses the source's subpolynomial bound using an exponent function o : ℕ → ℝ with o =o[atTop] 1 and an eventual inequality r(n) ≤ n^(o(n)). The website writes r(n)=n^{o(1)}; Erdős's original paper, p. 34, asks whether the representation count is o(n^ε).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The little-o condition on o is exactly o(n) → 0. For a nonnegative representation count r, existence of such an eventual exponent bound is equivalent to ∀ ε>0, eventually r(n) ≤ n^ε. Conversely, one can choose o(n)=log(max(r(n),1))/log(n) for n≥2. The epsilon-bound formulation is also equivalent to ∀ ε>0, r(n)=o(n^ε), using the ε/2 bound. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Nat.Powerful includes zero, so sumRep Powerful counts representations involving zero, whereas the usual powerful numbers are positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing r₊ for the count with positive summands and r₀ for the Lean count, r₊(n) ≤ r₀(n) ≤ r₊(n)+2: only (0,n) and (n,0) can be added. A bounded additive change preserves subpolynomial growth. The scratch file proves these bounds and the full ↔ between the theorem's right-hand side and the corresponding statement restricted to positive powerful summands.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #943, https://www.erdosproblems.com/943, read through archived copies: https://web.archive.org/web/20250901000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/943 and https://web.archive.org/web/20260824213257id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/943.
